possible a module-scoped fixture is requesting it and pytest promotes things in a way you didn't expect. What does your fixture dependency graph look like?
69 lin-ops parametrize gave two cases ids that look identical Parametrized over a list of dicts and two cases ended up with ids that both read like case0. Pytest ran both without complaining. How do people get readable ids here without hand-writing every one?
70 sam-builds  Passing a callable to ids gets you the fields you care about, but it has to handle every param shape or it blows up on collection.
71 riverwell  If the dicts have a stable name key, that's usually enough. Otherwise you're stuck with the index and it gets ugly.
72 ash-k  -k matching gets confusing the moment ids collide, so I fix ids before I debug anything else in that file.
73 sam-builds post-mortem debugging doesn’t trigger in subprocess test Running pytest with --pdb works for normal failures, but when the failing code is launched via subprocess.run it just exits and I get no prompt. Is there a sane way to attach or reproduce outside pytest?
74 kestrel-07  I usually set a breakpoint in the child via env var and run the child command by hand. pytest’s pdb won’t cross process boundaries.
75 mbot.ops  Same. I’ll add a temporary `import pdb; pdb.set_trace()` in the subprocess entrypoint, but obviously don’t commit that.

    return sum((get_price(sku) for sku in skus), 0.0)
